title: How the Golden Triangle is actually paced
excerpt: Delhi, Jaipur, and Agra in six nights is the programme most first-time visitors ask for. This is how C More runs those days.
body: The Golden Triangle is not three cities in a blur. On C More’s six-night plan, the first afternoon is New Delhi: Lutyens’ avenues, India Gate, Qutub Minar, and Humayun’s Tomb, with the room available from early afternoon so the drive from the airport is not wasted.

Jaipur takes the next two days. One afternoon is the city — City Palace, Jantar Mantar, a stop at Hawa Mahal, and the gem market. The following morning is Amber Fort, reached by elephant when the fort allows it and by jeep when it does not, then Jaigarh.

The road to Agra stops at Fatehpur Sikri. Agra itself keeps a full day for Sikandra, Agra Fort, and the Taj Mahal in the late afternoon, when the marble changes colour. The return to Delhi is used for Old Delhi: Red Fort, Chandni Chowk, Jama Masjid, and Raj Ghat.
The published price starts at USD 399 per person. Hotels, the exact guiding, and any extra night are confirmed in writing before a deposit is taken.

title: Pushkar Fair, and what the week contains
excerpt: The November cattle fair is a pilgrimage and a market at once. C More’s 10-night programme puts it between Jaipur and Agra.
body: Pushkar sits just beyond Ajmer, on a lake that Hindus treat as sacred. For a few days in Kartik, usually November, the sand fills with camels, horses, cattle, competitions, and stalls. C More treats it as a fair you stay inside, not a spectacle you drive past.

The published tour is 10 nights and 11 days, starting in Delhi and moving through Jaipur before the fair days. Mornings at the ghats, afternoons on the fairground, then the road continues toward Agra and the Taj.
The starting price on the current programme is USD 865 per person. Fair dates move with the lunar calendar, so the office confirms the exact week before hotels are held.

title: Plan your dream trip and book a Taj Mahal tour
excerpt: India is large, and the choices are many. C More’s published programmes start with the sights people actually fly for — beginning with the Taj.
body: India is a great country with interesting culture and history, several types of climate and geography, and many famous sights. Travelling here when you have saved for a long holiday is always remarkable, and it can also be daunting with the number of choices. A written tour that includes the Taj Mahal, run by an incoming office, is how most first visits are actually taken.

The first step is deciding when and where you want to go. Delhi, Agra, Jaipur, Mumbai, Goa, Kerala, and Rajasthan are among the places most visitors ask for. Plan ahead for the Taj, Varanasi, Amber Fort, and the Goa coast if that is the kind of trip you want.

India’s weather varies by season and by region. October to March is the dry, cooler window on the northern plains. July and August are monsoon in much of the country. C More will say which of its programmes sit in which months before a date is held.

Allow time for any domestic flights the itinerary needs. Hotel category and the exact days are confirmed in writing. The Golden Triangle programme, from USD 399, is the shortest published way to see Delhi, Jaipur, and Agra with a private car.

title: The mystique of Jaisalmer: why camel safari tours are so popular
excerpt: Camel safari in Jaisalmer is how many people first meet the Thar. C More’s Rajasthan programmes put a night in the dunes into a written desert route.
body: Camel safari tours in Jaisalmer draw visitors from around the world. The Thar Desert in Rajasthan is close enough to the sandstone city that a day on a camel still ends in a camp, not a long transfer. Jaisalmer, the Golden City, is built of the same stone as the dunes around it.

For ages people have used camels to cross this sand. The pace is slow enough to look properly. C More’s Camel Safari in Rajasthan tour (11 nights, from USD 745) puts Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Ranakpur, and Udaipur on one private circuit.
A safari is also a way to see how desert villages actually live: tea, folk music, and a meal that is not hotel food. Sunset on the dunes is the hour most people remember.

Overnight camps sit under a dark sky. Traditional Rajasthani cooking and local music are part of that night. Compared with a jeep-only circuit, a camel stretch has a lighter footprint. The office confirms whether the camp is for one night or two before you fly.
